project.name: Project Builder
project.purpose: Build a definition-first studio that turns domains into inspectable, testable, and eventually executable system models while keeping human workflows complete.

elements.name: Modeler
elements.description: Defines and inspects system meaning through human-complete workflows.

goals: Express system truth without inventing missing knowledge.

elements.name: Contributor
elements.description: Builds and verifies the Project Builder repository.

goals: Run, inspect, and verify a clean repository clone.
responsibilities: Preserve repository invariants and return reproducible evidence.

elements.name: Reviewer
elements.description: Evaluates definitions, implementation changes, and evidence.

goals: Determine whether delivered claims have persuasive evidence.
responsibilities: Review scope, architecture, model validity, and reproducibility.

elements.name: Repository Can Be Run and Verified
elements.description: A contributor can move from a clean clone to a healthy shell and the same deterministic checks used by CI.

payload.statement: A contributor can restore, build, test, run, and verify Project Builder from a clean clone using documented repository commands.
successSignals: The CI-equivalent verification command passes.
The application and PostgreSQL resource report healthy.

elements.name: Bootstrap Repository
elements.description: Establish the executable and evidence-producing repository foundation.

payload.start: A contributor has a clean clone and the documented local prerequisites.
payload.end: The shell is healthy and repository verification returns passing evidence.

elements.name: Clean Clone Is Built and Run
elements.description: The initial executable foundation path.

startingFacts: .NET SDK 10.0.303 or an allowed patch roll-forward is installed.

payload.trigger: The contributor runs the documented repository command.
payload.expectedOutcome: Project Builder opens, readiness is healthy, and the CI-equivalent verification succeeds.

elements.name: Domain Dependency Direction
elements.description: Semantic truth remains independent of mechanisms and presentation.

payload.statement: Domain cannot depend on Infrastructure or Presentation.
payload.falsifyingExample: ProjectBuilder.Domain adds a reference to ProjectBuilder.Infrastructure or an ASP.NET Core assembly.
proofExpectation: Architecture tests reject forbidden project and assembly references.

elements.name: Canonical Primitive Values Remain Valid

payload.statement: Foundational domain values are accepted only after explicit validation and serialize deterministically.

elements.name: Validate Canonical Primitive Values
elements.description: Construct immutable identities and primitive values through explicit accepted or rejected semantic results.

payload.ability: Validate external primitive values without relying on expected-input exceptions, infrastructure, serialization attributes, or ambient time.

elements.name: Project Purpose Is Persisted and Visible

elements.name: Create Project Definition

elements.name: Authorized Modeler Creates Project

elements.name: Modeler Inspects One Immutable Lens Graph

payload.statement: A modeler can trace one revision through a client-safe immutable lens contract without treating layout, selection, or filters as semantic truth.
successSignals: Equivalent inputs produce byte-identical lens responses and content hashes.
Every visible edge resolves through owned typed input and output ports.
Filtering pins project context, suppresses dangling edges, and emits an inspectable diagnostic.
Every visible node has a deterministic structured accessibility item.
Light, dark, and narrow Studio layouts preserve inspection and keyboard navigation.

elements.name: Project Revision into Typed Lens Contract

payload.ability: Project Project, Actor, Outcome, and their owned benefitsFrom relation into deterministic nodes, directional ports, edges, diagnostics, inspector schema, and accessibility order without storing layout.

elements.name: Modeler Traces Value through a Story Map
elements.description: A modeler can inspect explicit outcomes, capabilities, episodes, scenarios, scenes, and participants as one deterministic value-to-behavior projection without inferred semantic structure.

payload.statement: A modeler can follow modeled value into an explicit ability and narrative packet while projection layout and overlays remain view state.
successSignals: The same revision, filters, and overlays produce byte-identical story-map/1 responses and hashes.
A missing capability remains a visible diagnostic rather than inferred workflow truth.
Capability creation uses an expected-revision change set and references existing outcomes.
Every visible connector declares persisted, containment, or explicit-reference provenance.
Light, dark, narrow, keyboard, and structured views preserve the value-to-scene trace.

elements.name: Project Canonical Story Definitions into Outcome-Centered Map

elements.name: Reviewer Plays Every Modeled Scenario Path
elements.description: A reviewer can inspect and step through primary, exceptional, and recovery routes from explicit participants, conditions, ordered behavior, effects, boundary classifications, observations, and terminal results without executing production code.

payload.statement: A reviewer can follow authored behavior from trigger to expected outcome, switch to exceptional and recovery routes, and inspect exactly which nodes are semantic elements or derived explicit fields.
successSignals: The same project revision and scenario ID produce byte-identical scenario-flow/1 responses and hashes.
The primary route terminates once at its explicit expected outcome rather than treating every declared result as sequential behavior.
Exceptional and recovery paths preserve canonical condition, effect, result, and ordered-segment references.
ExternalInteraction effects produce an explicit classified boundary crossing; missing boundaries remain diagnostics.
Path tabs, playback controls, arrow keys, transcript, dark theme, and narrow layout expose equivalent authored truth.

elements.name: Project Typed Behavior into Playable Scenario Flow
elements.description: Project canonical narrative and path packets into deterministic participant lanes, typed nodes, explicit provenance, classified boundaries, terminal results, playback steps, and a structured equivalent.

payload.ability: Project Interaction, Intent, Step, Observation, Path, Condition, Effect, and Result identifiers plus explicit field fragments into validated read-only flow and playback contracts without storing layout or running target code.

elements.name: Reviewer Explains State and Rule Causality
elements.description: A reviewer can trace source and target predicates, the governing transition, changed facts, evaluated rules, preserved invariants, typed results, and explicit effects through equivalent graph and matrix forms.

payload.statement: A reviewer can switch among a causal graph, transition matrix, rule decision table, and invariant proof panel without recreating definitions or confusing unknown-capable facts with missing truth.
successSignals: The same project revision and state ID produce byte-identical state-rule/1 responses and hashes.
Transition references to facts, rules, invariants, and results remain stable semantic edges.
Source and target predicates declare derived-explicit-field provenance.
Missing event and effect definitions remain visible diagnostics rather than inferred nodes.
Graph, matrices, inspector, keyboard traversal, dark theme, and narrow layout expose equivalent authored truth.

elements.name: Project Typed State into Equivalent Rule Views

payload.ability: Project stable State, Fact, Rule, Invariant, Transition, Result, and explicit Effect references into validated read-only contracts without persisting representation or selection state.

elements.name: Reviewer Traces Accountable System Crossings
elements.description: A reviewer can inspect owned and external systems, interface intent, ownership and trust boundaries, governing contracts, and explicitly declared data movement in equivalent visual and structured forms.

successSignals: One expected-revision operation commits five typed definitions atomically.
The same revision, system ID, and overlay produce byte-identical system-context/1 responses and hashes.
Request and response data flow only from explicit Contract fields.
A corrupted projection endpoint fails validation.
Composer, topology, inspector, keyboard outline, light, dark, and narrow views remain equivalent.

elements.description: Commit an owned system, external system, interface, boundary, and contract atomically, then project explicit ownership, trust, effect, and data-movement references.

payload.ability: Define accountable system crossings through one typed expected-revision command and expose a validated read-only topology without persisting layout or overlay state.

elements.name: Reviewer Traces Promised Value to Current Proof

successSignals: A claim and evidence packet commits atomically at one expected revision.
The same revision and view produce byte-identical traceability/1 responses and hashes.
A later linked semantic change marks the evidence review-required.
Missing outcome links expose exact repair routes.
Composer, path river, debt view, impact radar, inspector, keyboard outline, light, dark, and narrow views remain equivalent.

elements.name: Modeler Navigates a Semantic Canvas Without Changing Truth

Wheel, keyboard, and visible zoom controls update bounded scale without a semantic revision.
Arrow-key and pointer selection synchronize the inspector and semantic outline.
Fit Scope, Fit Selection, Across, and Down commands expose view-only behavior.
Light, dark, reduced-motion-safe, and narrow layouts retain command and outline access.

elements.name: Operate Accessible SVG Model Viewports

payload.ability: Map an immutable lens projection into deterministic SVG geometry and bounded viewport interactions entirely inside Presentation while leaving persistence and semantic commands untouched.

claims.statement: A clean clone restores, builds, tests, and exposes a healthy Project Builder shell through documented commands.
Domain cannot depend on Infrastructure or Presentation.
Every accepted canonical identifier is non-empty and round-trips through canonical text.
An authorized modeler creates and reopens a purpose-led project at revision 1 through the browser.
Invalid project meaning returns visible semantic errors without erasing entered values.
Project creation is idempotent and queryable through the stable HTTP use-case contract backed by PostgreSQL.

A modeler commits and reviews typed project-creation state and logic through one expected-revision change set and the stable API.
A modeler commits and reviews an exceptional branch and reciprocal owned recovery through one expected-revision change set and the stable API.
A modeler reviews an executable relation descriptor while invalid endpoint and cardinality combinations cannot become committed model truth.
Every accepted model transition persists one atomic ordered typed change set; stale and idempotently repeated commands cannot overwrite or duplicate state.

A modeler imports a supported format-1.0 project atomically or defines the compatible profile natively, then exports a schema-valid deterministic snapshot, while unsafe, future-version, stale, and unsupported state fails closed.

A contributor enters a stable theme-aware studio shell, reaches the work surface by keyboard, retains usable navigation at narrow width, and recovers from an unknown location without changing semantic state.
A modeler opens a project outcome cockpit, sees explicit current gaps and one deterministic next action, and reaches history review after all currently supported typed packets are present.
A modeler filters a virtualized semantic tree, retains focus, selects a typed definition through a stable URL, reorders the view without drag or semantic mutation, and opens contextual detail.
A contributor stages actor meaning in a typed Studio editor, sees validation, source limitations, uncertainty, and command metadata, then commits the actor through one expected-revision change set.

A contributor compares duplicate actor and outcome suggestions, commits a beneficiary-linked observable outcome, updates actor and outcome meaning, retargets the relation atomically, and recovers a stale draft without losing input.

A contributor authors a complete ordered narrative through a responsive flow studio, reviews participants, direction, path, references, readiness, and semantic operations, then commits one atomic expected-revision change set.

A contributor authors the reference POS state model through a responsive State Lens, reviews categorized truth, authority, rule and invariant constraints, transition topology, typed results, and path status, then commits one atomic expected-revision change set without raw JSON.

A reviewer opens an intentionally incomplete model, filters its deterministic Problems catalog, inspects rule, severity, Open status, owner and exact scope, reviews Unknown evidence requirements, and navigates into an existing repair command without invented lifecycle mutation.

A contributor stages typed Actor, Outcome, Narrative, State, and Recovery drafts, uses bounded undo and redo, reloads to recover them, explicitly reconciles stale bases, commits through scoped keyboard commands, and inspects canonical semantic operations in accessible themed layouts.

A contributor authors a complete typed branch and recovery through a visual topology, uses Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y without global input injection, reloads to recover the draft, commits with Ctrl+S, and reviews the result through light, dark, and responsive interfaces.

A reviewer switches an incomplete model between Discovery and Implementation Ready, sees purpose-relative severities and prerequisite-aware coverage, then records an accountable disposition whose authority, rationale, consequence, review gate, audit reason, and revision remain visible without claiming semantic repair.

A contributor sees a deterministic, versioned guidance map whose applicable prompts explain their current-fact trigger, rationale, learning context, answer-to-change mappings, and repair route; invalid or unreachable prompts fail registry validation without pretending an answer was persisted.

A contributor navigates a non-modal contextual Guide Rail, records explicit local answer state, closes and reopens with Ctrl+Shift+G or Escape, returns to the same prompt after reload, and retains the invoking focus target while the canonical revision remains unchanged.

A novice uses plain-language Guide Rail prompts to recover and commit an accountable participant, select that existing meaning as beneficiary, commit an observable outcome and benefitsFrom relation atomically, inspect the revision history, and continue to the next deterministically applicable behavior prompt.

Given a newly created POS project with typed participants and outcome, a novice uses the Guide Rail to recover and commit the ordinary recognized-item scan from starting facts and trigger through Episode, Scenario, Scene, directed Interaction, Intent, Step, Observation, and semantic results, then inspects the canonical revision history.

Given the same canonical revision, purpose profile, versioned rules, findings, dependencies, and recent work, the recommendation API is byte-stable; changing only the purpose profile changes declared pressure without changing model truth, blocked dependencies remain blocked, and the Decision Lens explains and follows the selected action.

Given Project Builder discovery facts at one revision, a facilitator runs all six deterministic workshop movements, captures owned provisional Decision, Assumption, and Question notes plus a parked thread, reloads without losing matching-revision progress, presents a control-free participant view, and exports the revision-attributed workshop record without changing canonical model truth.

Given one canonical project revision, the lens API returns byte-identical typed topology; a modeler inspects semantic nodes and ports, filters without dangling edges, sees suppression diagnostics, follows the structured keyboard path, and receives equivalent light, dark, and responsive Studio views without changing model truth.

Given explicit outcome and participant truth, a modeler sees a missing-capability diagnostic, commits an outcome-linked capability with expected revision, adds an owned narrative packet, and traces value through capability, episode, scenario, scene, and actors in deterministic light, dark, responsive, keyboard, and structured views.

Given a typed primary scenario plus exceptional and recovery path packets, a reviewer opens Scenario Flow, steps the primary route by keyboard, switches paths, plays to terminal results, inspects an explicit external-interaction boundary, and receives equivalent transcript, structured, light, dark, and responsive projections without model mutation or production execution.

Given typed state, fact, rule, invariant, transition, and semantic-result definitions, a reviewer opens State and Rule, traverses the causal graph by keyboard, switches to transition, decision, and invariant representations, inspects unknown capability and no-inference findings, and receives equivalent light, dark, responsive, structured, and byte-stable projections.

Given distinct owned and external authorities, a modeler composes one typed system-context packet, commits it at the expected revision, and a reviewer inspects explicit ownership, trust, contract data flow, deterministic projection provenance, keyboard structure, and theme-aware responsive views.

Given a material outcome, a contributor attaches an explicitly scoped claim and evidence packet; a reviewer then inspects supported paths, evidence debt, and revision-relative change impact through equivalent keyboard, light, dark, and responsive views.

Given a deterministic typed lens projection, a modeler selects nodes, pans and zooms the viewport, fits scope and selection, changes view-only alignment, and inspects the synchronized semantic outline through pointer and keyboard-equivalent operations without changing canonical revision.
Given a deterministic canvas layout, a modeler saves distinct personal and team view definitions, reloads either view, and resets presentation state without advancing the canonical semantic revision.

Given a selected semantic definition, a modeler opens it as a focused scope through keyboard or visible commands, retains pinned parent context and explicit cross-scope stubs, and restores the same location through deep links and browser back or forward navigation.

Given an authored scenario with primary, exceptional, and recovery paths linked to explicit state and invariant definitions, a reviewer plays, pauses, steps, selects branches, inspects state and participant observations, and stops for invariant review without executing target behavior or inferring truth.
